title: getSourceFile().moduleName is undefined
author: alan-agius4

comments.body:
You actually want to use `file.fileName`.

`moduleName` is something related to AMD modules. But that comment is not present in the generated declaration files.
Is there anyway to get the moduleName ie: 'jasmine' in any other way?

satisfaction_conditions: A way to determine which module (specifically 'jasmine') a function or expression comes from
A method to identify ambient module declarations when direct imports aren't available
A way to match function declarations to their source modules
An alternative to the non-functional moduleName property

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

git_commit_info.message: Added deferred ScriptKind and renamed JsFileExtensionInfo to FileExtensionInfo
git_commit_info.author: Armando Aguirre

dockerfile:
FROM node:14-slim

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies needed for building TypeScript
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the repository and checkout the specific commit
RUN git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript.git . && \
    git checkout 50eb5125664d47ac7cb59a2889236f200a4f4c7d

# Install specific versions of dependencies that work with this older TypeScript version
# Pinning versions to avoid compatibility issues
RUN npm install --no-package-lock
RUN npm install --no-package-lock del@5.1.0 globby@10.0.2

# Create the missing scripts directory and file
RUN mkdir -p scripts && \
    touch scripts/generateLocalizedDiagnosticMessages.js

# Copy the built JS files from lib/ to built/local/ to simulate the build
RUN mkdir -p built/local && \
    cp lib/*.js built/local/

# Create a workspace directory for the user to test the issue
WORKDIR /workspace

# Create test files to reproduce the issue
RUN echo 'it("should", () => "");' > index.ts && \
    echo 'import * as ts from "typescript";\n\
\n\
const program = ts.createProgram(["./index.ts"], { types: ["jasmine"] });\n\
const sourceFile = program.getSourceFile("./index.ts");\n\
const checker = program.getTypeChecker();\n\
\n\
ts.forEachChild(sourceFile, checkNested);\n\
\n\
function checkNested(node: ts.Node) {\n\
  if (ts.isCallExpression(node)) {\n\
    const signature = checker.getResolvedSignature(node);\n\
    const file = signature.getDeclaration().getSourceFile();\n\
\n\
    console.log("fileName:", file.fileName);\n\
    console.log("moduleName:", file.moduleName);\n\
  }\n\
\n\
  ts.forEachChild(node, checkNested);\n\
}' > checker.ts

# Create a package.json file for the workspace
RUN echo '{\n\
  "name": "typescript-issue-test",\n\
  "version": "1.0.0",\n\
  "description": "Test for TypeScript issue #23195",\n\
  "dependencies": {\n\
    "typescript": "file:/app"\n\
  },\n\
  "devDependencies": {\n\
    "jasmine": "^3.0.0",\n\
    "@types/jasmine": "^2.8.0"\n\
  }\n\
}' > package.json

# Install workspace dependencies
RUN npm install

# Setup the PATH to include the TypeScript binaries
ENV PATH="/app/bin:${PATH}"

# Command to keep container running
CMD ["tail", "-f", "/dev/null"]
